item: River intake - gated openings to river
quote: The intake structure has four gated openings to the North Umpqua River, each 4 feet square.
value: 4 openings, each 4x4 ft

quote: There are two traveling screens which screen the raw water before it enters the pump bay. These screens will pass up to 18 mgd or more of raw water.
value: up to 18 mgd or more (2 screens)

item: River intake - openings screens to pump bay
quote: There are two 5 feet square gated openings between the traveling screens and the pump bay. These openings are of adequate size to supply the intake pumps with up to 24 mgd or more
value: 2 openings, each 5x5 ft, adequate to 24 mgd or more

quote: These openings are of adequate size to supply the intake pumps with up to 24 mgd or more of raw water.
value: 4x4-ft openings adequate to 24 mgd or more (hydraulically, before fish-velocity limit)

quote: The maximum velocity in the intake outside the traveling screens occurs at the 4 feet square gated openings. As discussed in Section 3, because these openings are located outside the fish screens, the maximum approach velocity for protection of fish applies at these openings. With a maximum approach velocity of 0.4 fps and with the gates fully submerged
value: 0.4 fps max approach at 4-ft openings, gates fully submerged

item: Raw water pump station - 2006 demonstrated capacity 3 pumps
quote: On September 14, 2006 with Pump Nos. 1, 2 and 4 operating, the intake provided only 14 mgd.
value: 14 mgd with Pump Nos. 1,2,4 operating

item: Raw water pump station - 2002 firm capacity test
quote: Testing of the station in 2002 determined that the firm capacity of the station at that time was approximately 15.0 mgd.
value: approx 15.0 mgd firm (2002)

quote: The 2002 test results appear to indicate that Pump No. 3 is pumping substantially below its rated capacity; however, Pump No. 3 was not operating during the test on September 14, 2006 and the capacity was even lower.
value: Pump No.3 substantially below rated (2002); not operating 2006 yet capacity lower

quote: The City recently installed a VFD on Pump No. 2.
value: VFD on Pump No.2 installed; plus VFDs on one raw and one finished pump being installed per p.115

item: Raw water pipeline - diameter, material, wall
quote: The raw water pumps discharge into an underground 30-inch diameter steel raw water pipeline ... The steel pipe has a 1/4-inch wall thickness.
value: 30-in steel, 1/4-in wall

quote: A 30-inch magnetic flow meter was installed on this pipeline in a below-grade vault in 2002
value: 30-in mag meter (2002)

quote: TABLE 4-1 30-INCH RAW WATER PIPELINE VELOCITIES AND HEADLOSS Plant Flow (mgd) Velocity (fps) V2/2g (ft) Headloss (ft/100 ft) 8 2.6 0.116 0.05; 12 3.9 0.24 0.11; 18 5.9 0.54 0.25; 20 6.5 0.66 0.32; 24 7.8 0.90 0.44
As shown in the table, velocities through the 30-inch raw water pipeline exceed 6.0 fps at flows slightly over 18 mgd.
value: >6.0 fps slightly over 18 mgd

item: Rapid mix basins - two parallel, one operated
quote: There are two rapid mix basins in parallel, but currently only one rapid mixer is operated at any given time.
value: 2 basins parallel, 1 operated currently

quote: Under those conditions, both rapid mix basins will be operated in parallel at the higher flows.
value: both basins in parallel at higher (18 mgd) flows

quote: The single existing basin is rated at 12 mgd
value: 12 mgd single basin

quote: was designed to be expanded with a parallel basin for an ultimate nominal treatment capacity of 18 mgd, but with approximately 24 mgd of hydraulic capacity.
value: 18 mgd nominal, ~24 mgd hydraulic (2 basins)

quote: this basin has been able to provide excellent pretreatment prior to filtration at sustained flows up to 11.5 mgd during the warm weather, low turbidity raw water conditions.
value: up to 11.5 mgd sustained demonstrated

quote: Normal plant flows during high turbidity, colder water conditions have ranged from 3.5 to 5.0 mgd.

item: Sed basin launder weir and trough elevations
quote: There is a triangular launder weir in the sedimentation basin with invert elevation of approximately 465.83 feet. The bottoms of the 12-inch deep launder troughs in the sedimentation basin are approximately elevation 464.63 feet.
value: launder weir invert ~465.83; trough bottoms ~464.63 (12-in deep troughs)

quote: The freeboard from the top of maximum water surface to the top of walls is approximately 1.5 feet which is adequate.
value: ~1.5 ft adequate

item: Sed basin overflow weir elevation and relation to filters
quote: The overflow weir elevation is at 465.0 feet, approximately 1.0 feet higher than the normal filter operating level.
value: 465.0 ft, ~1.0 ft above normal filter level

item: Sed basin overflow weir length and capacity
quote: The weir is approximately 9 feet long with a capacity of approximately 12 mgd, assuming a 9-inch water depth over the weir.
value: ~9 ft long, ~12 mgd at 9-in depth

item: Sed basin overflow drain pipe capacity and routing
quote: The drain pipe is 30-inches in diameter, has a capacity of approximately 10 mgd, and delivers this flow to a diversion manhole with a weir. Under normal conditions sedimentation basin overflows are directed to the wastewater pump station, but if the pump station cannot handle the flow the water flows over the weir inside the diversion manhole and then to the river.
value: 30-in drain ~10 mgd to diversion MH with weir; normal to WWPS, excess to river

quote: A second overflow weir will be constructed along with the second flocculation/sedimentation basin when the plant is expanded; thus, the overflow system is adequate for an ultimate maximum plant capacity of 24 mgd.
value: 2 weirs adequate to 24 mgd ultimate max

item: Settled water pipeline to filters - diameter and velocities
quote: The settled water pipeline to the filters is a 42-inch diameter steel pipe. At 18 mgd the pipeline velocity will be 2.9 fps and at 24 mgd the pipeline velocity would be 3.9 fps.
value: 42-in steel; 2.9 fps at 18 mgd, 3.9 fps at 24 mgd

item: Settled water pipeline - measured headloss and channel level
quote: During a flow test conducted on September 14, 2006, the head loss through the pipe was measured at 2.8-inches at a flow rate of 13.1 mgd. Under these conditions, the water surface in the settled water channel was approximately 6-inches below the basin overflow weir.
value: 2.8-in HL at 13.1 mgd; WS ~6-in below overflow weir (i.e. ~464.5 ft vs 465.0 ft)

item: Settled water pipeline limits two-basin ultimate
quote: The ultimate hydraulic capacity of the two basins in parallel is limited primarily by the settled water pipeline and that ultimate capacity is 22 to 24 mgd.
value: 22-24 mgd (settled-water-pipe limited)

quote: Settled water flows through the filter influent channel and enters each filter via a 20-inch pipe with isolation valve.
value: influent channel + 20-in pipe with valve per filter

quote: The normal filter operating level ranges from 463 to 464 feet

with ... a raw water flow of 9.1 mgd, the flow through filter No. 1 in filter-to-waste was estimated ... The filter-to-waste flow was approximately 2 mgd while the flow through the other two filters was greater than 3.4 mgd.
value: at 9.1 mgd raw: ~2 mgd to waste (Filter 1), >3.4 mgd each through Filters 2 and 4

quote: Unbaffled area under the four filters with a maximum storage volume of approximately 170,000 gallons at 10.5 foot water depth.
value: ~170,000 gal at 10.5 ft (unbaffled, 4 filters)

quote: Baffled clearwell area underneath the chemical rooms and the blower room with a maximum storage volume of approximately 324,000 gallons at 10.5 foot water depth.
value: ~324,000 gal at 10.5 ft (baffled)

item: Clearwell zone 3 under HS pump room
quote: Unbaffled area underneath the high service pump room with a maximum storage volume of approximately 133,000 gallon at 10.5 foot water depth.
value: ~133,000 gal at 10.5 ft (unbaffled)

item: Clearwell total storage and time at current max
quote: The total maximum treated water storage volume of 627,000 gallons represents approximately 75 minutes (1.26 hours) of storage at the current maximum
value: 627,000 gal = ~75 min (1.26 hr) at current max

quote: The clearwell level control is accomplished by manually throttling valves on the discharge piping of a raw water pump and a finished water pump
value: manual throttling of raw + finished pump discharges

item: Finished water header and site main
quote: discharge into a steel header ... varies in diameter from 18-inch diameter at the east end to 30-inch diameter at the west end. ... The finished water transmission pipeline wall is 3/8-inch thick and the inside diameter is 29.25-inches.
value: 18-in to 30-in header; buried main ID 29.25-in, 3/8-in wall

item: Finished water Table 4-3 site main velocities/headloss
quote: TABLE 4-3 30-INCH FINISHED WATER TRANSMISSION MAIN VELOCITIES AND HEADLOSS Plant Flow (mgd) Velocity (fps) V2/2g (ft) Headloss (ft/100 ft) 8 2.65 0.109 0.05; 12 3.98 0.246 0.11; 18 5.97 0.553 0.25; 20 6.63 0.682 0.32; 24 7.96 0.984 0.44

This small headloss increase is not significant within the total finished water transmission system headloss. Replacing pumps with a higher pumping head may be necessary to overcome the entire system headloss if an ultimate plant flow of greater than 18 mgd is to be provided, but not because of the small added headloss associated with this short transmission main segment.
value: short site segment HL small; higher head may be needed >18 mgd for entire system

quote: The 1,900 cubic feet (14,200-gallon) tank was designed to provide both upsurge and downsurge protection

item: Surge protection flow and pressure criteria
quote: Surge protection is provided for pumping rates up to 9,700 gpm (14.0 mgd) The maximum upsurge in the transmission pipeline between plant and terminal reservoirs is controlled to 150 psi. The minimum allowable downsurge at the high service pump station is controlled to an HGL of 630 feet (approximately 175 feet of head or 75 psi assuming plant ground elevation of 455 feet.)
value: up to 9,700 gpm (14.0 mgd); max upsurge 150 psi; min downsurge HGL 630 ft (~175 ft head / 75 psi at ground 455 ft)

quote: The addition of a second hydropneumatic surge tank is likely not practical due to space constraints at the site.
value: second tank likely not practical - space

item: Northerly transmission to reservoirs - existing mains
quote: These mains are a 20-inch outside diameter steel main with a 3/16-inch thick wall and a 30-inch diameter Class 50 ductile iron main.
value: 20-in OD steel (3/16-in wall) + 30-in Class 50 DI

quote: Phase 1 consisted of construction of approximately 9,400 feet of new parallel transmission piping and demolition of an existing booster pumping station. Phase 2 consisted of the easterly and southerly extension of a new 27-inch diameter transmission main approximately 1,600 feet long ... it is anticipated that a new 30-inch main will be constructed initially ... to replace the existing 27-inch main. A second parallel 30-inch main would be constructed in the future
value: Ph1 ~9,400 ft parallel; Ph2 ~1,600 ft 27-in, now anticipated 30-in initially + 2nd parallel 30-in future

item: Air scour blower and air piping
quote: The blower has a capacity of 1,050 scfm at 6.4 psi and is driven by a 60 hp motor. Low pressure air is directed to each of the filters through an 8-inch diameter air supply system.
value: 1,050 scfm at 6.4 psi, 60 hp, 8-in air supply

quote: two constant-speed vertical turbine backwash pumps, each with a 50 hp motor, rated at 3,250 gpm at 41 feet TDH. Only one pump is required for backwashing each of the filter bays. The second pump serves as a spare/backup
value: 2x 3,250 gpm at 41 ft TDH, 50 hp; 1 duty, 1 spare

quote: The backwash pumps discharge into a 16-inch diameter header that feeds backwash water to the individual filters. These pumps and the associated piping and valving are adequately sized for the existing filter configuration and filter type.
value: 16-in header adequate for existing config/type

item: Deep-bed future backwash rate vs test
quote: It is estimated that the optimum backwash rate for these filter bays outfitted with deep bed media (up to 1.1 mm effective size anthracite) would be approximately 4,400 gpm. When the pumps were tested on September 14, 2006 with the modulating butterfly valve at approximately 45 deg open, the pumps produced 4,060 gpm
value: optimum ~4,400 gpm for deep bed to 1.1 mm; tested 4,060 gpm at 45-deg open

quote: Filter backwash water from each filter discharges through a 16-inch backwash drain pipeline into the backwash conveyance channel under the filter gallery floor slab. From the channel, flow is conveyed via a 24-inch diameter pipeline to a drain manhole and then through a 30-inch pipeline to the wastewater pump station. The new, larger pipeline will be capable of conveying a higher backwash flow in the future
value: 16-in per filter to channel, 24-in to MH, 30-in to WWPS (new larger, capable of higher future rate)

quote: three 35 hp submersible solids handling pumps, each with a capacity of approximately 1,500 gpm at 40 feet of TDH. Each pump has a 10-inch diameter discharge with 10-inch isolation and check valves.
value: 3x ~1,500 gpm at 40 ft TDH, 35 hp, 10-in discharge/valves

item: Wastewater transfer main and firm capacity
quote: A 16-inch diameter transfer main carries the wastewater to backwash basins 1 and 2. The approximate firm capacity of this station is 3,000 gpm with one of the pumps out of service.
value: 16-in transfer main; ~3,000 gpm firm (1 out)

item: Washwater/solids basins volume and drying beds
quote: Two new washwater and solids equalization/settling basins, plus the two new solids drying beds, were recently constructed ... Each basin has a maximum volume of approximately 300,000 gallons.
value: 2 basins x ~300,000 gal max + 2 drying beds

item: Plant operating regime and recent flow range
quote: The plant currently operates continuously throughout each day on a 24/7 basis ... The plant flow rate has ranged from approximately 3.5 mgd during low demand periods to 11.6 mgd during a recent peak summer day.
value: 24/7 to keep Reservoir Hill reservoirs full; 3.5 to 11.6 mgd range
